learning_objective: 🎯 Polish your grammar! Master the rules of tenses and learn to flip sentences without changing their core meaning.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: There are 3 main times (Present, Past, Future) and 4 states (Simple, Continuous, Perfect, Perfect Continuous), making 12 tenses total. E.g., 'I eat' (Simple), 'I am eating' (Continuous), 'I have eaten' (Perfect).
It is changing the grammatical structure of a sentence WITHOUT changing its actual meaning. (e.g., 'He is a good boy' -> 'He is not a bad boy').
To make a positive sentence negative without changing the meaning, use 'Not + Opposite word'. (e.g., 'Always speak the truth' -> 'Never tell a lie').
Sentences with 'too' are transformed using 'so...that'. E.g., 'He is too weak to walk' becomes 'He is so weak that he cannot walk'.
A statement can be turned into a rhetorical question to mean the same thing. E.g., 'Blood is thicker than water' -> 'Is blood not thicker than water?'.

fun_activity.title: 🔄 The Opposite Game
fun_activity.instructions: Transform this affirmative sentence into a negative one without changing its meaning: 'Every cloud has a silver lining.' (Hint: 'There is no cloud without...')

exam_tips: 📌 When transforming, the meaning must remain 100% identical. If the meaning changes, the answer is wrong.
📌 Pay special attention to tense agreement (If the first half is past tense, the second half usually must be past tense).
📌 Remember the rule: 'No sooner... than' and 'Hardly... when'.
quick_recap: ⭐ 'As soon as' is transformed to 'No sooner did/had... than'.
⭐ Perfect Continuous tenses always need a time marker ('since' for point in time, 'for' for duration).
